title: Inevitable, unavoidable, deserved
summary: Patterns of necessity and judgement: 'will inevitably' ({ずにはおかない}), 'can't get away without' ({ずにはすまない}), 'be forced to' ({を余儀[よぎ]なくされる}), grudging possibility, 'easy to imagine', 'worthy of', and 'deserves to'.

points.title: 〜ずにはおかない
points.meaning: will inevitably (cause); can't fail to; will definitely (do)
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + ずにはおかない (する → せずにはおかない)
points.explanation:
{〜ずにはおかない} literally means 'will not leave things without doing X'. Two uses:

**1. Inevitable effect (most common):** the subject is a thing — a film, a remark, a policy — and it will inevitably cause a reaction. Often with causative verbs: {感動[かんどう]させずにはおかない} 'can't fail to move people', {批判[ひはん]を招[まね]かずにはおかない} 'is bound to draw criticism'.

**2. Strong determination:** a person declares they will definitely do something: {犯人[はんにん]を捕[つか]まえずにはおかない} 'I will catch the culprit, no matter what'.

**Register:** formal and written — reviews, editorials, news commentary. The variant {〜ないではおかない} means the same.

examples.jp: この映画[えいが]は、見[み]る人[ひと]を感動[かんどう]させずにはおかない。
examples.en: This film cannot fail to move whoever watches it.

examples.jp: 今度[こんど]こそ、犯人[はんにん]を捕[つか]まえずにはおかない。
examples.en: This time, I'm going to catch the culprit, no matter what.

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しい税制[ぜいせい]は、国民[こくみん]の生活[せいかつ]に影響[えいきょう]を与[あた]えずにはおかない。
examples.en: The new tax system is bound to affect people's lives.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の無責任[むせきにん]な発言[はつげん]は、世間[せけん]の批判[ひはん]を招[まね]かずにはおかないだろう。
examples.en: His irresponsible remarks will inevitably draw public criticism.

points.notes: Compare {〜ずにはいられない} 'I can't help doing' (the speaker's own uncontrollable urge). {ずにはおかない} is about an unstoppable effect on others, or an iron will.

quiz.q: 彼女[かのじょ]の歌声[うたごえ]は、聞[き]く人[ひと]の心[こころ]を動[うご]かさ＿＿。
quiz.en: Her singing voice cannot fail to move the hearts of those who hear it.

quiz.q: この事件[じけん]は、社会[しゃかい]に大[おお]きな衝撃[しょうげき]を与[あた]え＿＿だろう。
quiz.en: This incident is bound to send a great shock through society.

points.title: 〜ずにはすまない／〜ないではすまない
points.meaning: won't get away without doing; will have to (by social obligation)
points.structure: Verb ない-stem + ずにはすまない / Verb ない-form + ではすまない (する → せずにはすまない)
points.explanation:
{すむ} means 'to be settled, to be over'. {〜ずにはすまない} means 'the matter won't be settled unless X is done' — i.e. given the situation, social norms or common sense demand that you do X. You broke something, so you'll have to pay; you caused trouble, so you'll have to apologise.

The obligation comes from the situation, not from the speaker's personal desire.

**Register:** formal; used in writing and in serious conversation. The variant {〜ないではすまない} is slightly more conversational. A related form is {〜ではすまない} 'won't end at X' ({謝[あやま]るだけではすまない} 'an apology alone won't be enough').

examples.jp: 大切[たいせつ]な書類[しょるい]をなくしたのだから、部長[ぶちょう]に謝[あやま]らずにはすまない。
examples.en: I lost important documents, so I'll have to apologise to the department head.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]の車[くるま]を傷[きず]つけてしまった。弁償[べんしょう]せずにはすまないだろう。
examples.en: I damaged my friend's car. I'll probably have to pay for it.

examples.jp: 嘘[うそ]がばれた以上[いじょう]、本当[ほんとう]のことを話[はな]さないではすまない。
examples.en: Now that the lie has come out, I'll have no choice but to tell the truth.

examples.jp: これほどの事故[じこ]を起[お]こした以上[いじょう]、会社[かいしゃ]の責任[せきにん]が問[と]われずにはすまないだろう。
examples.en: Having caused an accident this serious, the company is bound to be held responsible.

points.notes: {ずにはおかない} = something will inevitably cause an effect (or iron will); {ずにはすまない} = the situation obliges you to do something.

quiz.q: 約束[やくそく]を破[やぶ]って迷惑[めいわく]をかけたのだから、直接[ちょくせつ]会[あ]って謝[あやま]ら＿＿。
quiz.en: I broke my promise and caused trouble, so I'll have to meet them in person and apologise.

quiz.q: 会社[かいしゃ]のお金[かね]を使[つか]い込[こ]んだのだから、処分[しょぶん]を受[う]けないでは＿＿。
quiz.en: Since he embezzled company money, he won't get away without being disciplined.

points.title: 〜を余儀[よぎ]なくされる
points.meaning: to be forced to; to have no choice but to
points.structure: Noun (action) + を余儀[よぎ]なくされる / Noun + を余儀[よぎ]なくさせる (to force)
points.explanation:
{余儀[よぎ]ない} means 'unavoidable, no other option'. {X を余儀[よぎ]なくされる} means 'to be forced (by circumstances) into X' — typically something unwelcome like cancellation, withdrawal, retirement, closure or evacuation. X is a noun, usually a Sino-Japanese action noun: {中止[ちゅうし]}, {欠航[けっこう]}, {撤退[てったい]}, {閉鎖[へいさ]}, {引退[いんたい]}, {避難[ひなん]}.

The active form {〜を余儀[よぎ]なくさせる} puts the cause as the subject: 'the typhoon forced the cancellation'.

**Register:** very formal, and **extremely common in news**. You'll hear it on NHK every week. In conversation, you'd say {〜しなければならなくなった}.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]はけがのため、引退[いんたい]を余儀[よぎ]なくされた。
examples.en: He was forced to retire because of injury.

examples.jp: 台風[たいふう]の影響[えいきょう]で、多[おお]くの便[びん]が欠航[けっこう]を余儀[よぎ]なくされた。
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, many flights had to be cancelled.

examples.jp: 業績[ぎょうせき]の悪化[あっか]により、同社[どうしゃ]は工場[こうじょう]の閉鎖[へいさ]を余儀[よぎ]なくされた。
examples.en: Due to deteriorating results, the company was forced to close the factory.

examples.jp: 突然[とつぜん]の豪雨[ごうう]が、大会[たいかい]の中止[ちゅうし]を余儀[よぎ]なくさせた。
examples.en: The sudden downpour forced the tournament to be called off.

points.notes: The forced action is generally negative and caused by external circumstances (weather, the economy, injury), not by a person's order.

quiz.q: 大雪[おおゆき]のため、新幹線[しんかんせん]は運転[うんてん]見合[みあ]わせ＿＿。
quiz.en: Due to heavy snow, the Shinkansen was forced to suspend operations.
choices: を禁[きん]じ得[え]なかった
を皮切[かわき]りにした
を余儀[よぎ]なくされた
をものともしなかった

quiz.q: 資金[しきん]不足[ぶそく]により、研究[けんきゅう]チームは計画[けいかく]の変更[へんこう]を余儀[よぎ]なく＿＿。
quiz.en: Due to a lack of funds, the research team was forced to change its plans.

points.title: 〜ないものでもない
points.meaning: it's not impossible that; might (just) (if conditions are right)
points.structure: Verb ない-form + ものでもない / ものでもありません
points.explanation:
A double negative: {〜ないものでもない} means 'it's not the case that X can't/won't happen'. It expresses a reluctant, hedged possibility: 'I might be willing, depending on the conditions', 'we might just make it if we hurry'.

It often comes with a condition: {条件[じょうけん]次第[しだい]では}, {急[いそ]げば}, {〜があれば}. The speaker is cautious and not committing.

**Register:** somewhat formal and a little roundabout; used in negotiations and in careful speech or writing. The everyday equivalent is {〜ないこともない}, which is much more common.

examples.jp: 条件[じょうけん]次第[しだい]では、引[ひ]き受[う]けないものでもない。
examples.en: Depending on the terms, I might be willing to take it on.

examples.jp: 急[いそ]げば、最終[さいしゅう]電車[でんしゃ]に間[ま]に合[あ]わないものでもない。
examples.en: If we hurry, we might just make the last train.

examples.jp: 誠意[せいい]ある謝罪[しゃざい]があれば、許[ゆる]さないものでもない。
examples.en: If I get a sincere apology, I might be willing to forgive him.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の気持[きも]ちも分[わ]からないものでもないが、やはり規則[きそく]は規則[きそく]だ。
examples.en: It's not that I don't understand how he feels, but rules are rules.

points.notes: Learn {〜ないこともない} as the spoken version: {行[い]かないこともないけど…} 'I might go, I suppose...'.

quiz.q: 三日[みっか]あれば、できない＿＿が、確約[かくやく]はできない。
quiz.en: If I had three days, it might not be impossible, but I can't promise anything.

quiz.q: 君[きみ]がそこまで言[い]うなら、手伝[てつだ]ってあげない＿＿。
quiz.en: If you insist that much, I suppose I might help you.

points.title: 〜にかたくない
points.meaning: it is not hard to (imagine / understand)
points.structure: Noun (想像[そうぞう]・理解[りかい]) + にかたくない / Verb (察[さっ]する) + にかたくない
points.explanation:
{かたい} here is {難[かた]い} 'difficult' (an old, written word). {〜にかたくない} means 'it is not difficult to X' — and in practice the X is almost always imagining or understanding: {想像[そうぞう]にかたくない} 'easy to imagine', {察[さっ]するにかたくない} 'easy to guess (someone's feelings)', {理解[りかい]にかたくない}.

It's used when the speaker infers something (often someone's suffering, or a likely future consequence) from the situation.

**Register:** formal and written — editorials, essays, news commentary. {想像[そうぞう]にかたくない} is by far the most common form; learn it as a set phrase.

examples.jp: 彼女[かのじょ]がどれほど緊張[きんちょう]していたかは、想像[そうぞう]にかたくない。
examples.en: It's easy to imagine how nervous she must have been.

examples.jp: 突然[とつぜん]家族[かぞく]を失[うしな]った彼[かれ]の悲[かな]しみは、想像[そうぞう]にかたくない。
examples.en: It's not hard to imagine his grief at suddenly losing his family.

examples.jp: 一人[ひとり]で三人[さんにん]の子[こ]どもを育[そだ]てる苦労[くろう]は、察[さっ]するにかたくない。
examples.en: One can easily imagine the hardship of raising three children alone.

examples.jp: このまま値上[ねあ]げが続[つづ]けば、消費者[しょうひしゃ]の反発[はんぱつ]が強[つよ]まることは想像[そうぞう]にかたくない。
examples.en: If prices keep rising like this, it's easy to imagine consumer backlash growing.

points.notes: Don't use it with everyday verbs: {✕このパンは食[た]べるにかたくない}. It's reserved for imagining and understanding.

quiz.q: 被災者[ひさいしゃ]の不安[ふあん]は、想像[そうぞう]＿＿。
quiz.en: It's not hard to imagine the anxiety of the disaster victims.
choices: を余儀[よぎ]なくされる

quiz.q: 初[はじ]めて一人[ひとり]で海外[かいがい]に出[で]た娘[むすめ]の心細[こころぼそ]さは、察[さっ]する＿＿かたくない。
quiz.en: It's easy to imagine how lonely my daughter felt going abroad alone for the first time.

points.title: 〜に足[た]る／〜に足[た]りない
points.meaning: worthy of; enough to justify / not worth
points.structure: Verb (dictionary form) / Noun + に足[た]る (+ Noun) / に足[た]りない
points.explanation:
{足[た]る} is the classical form of {足[た]りる} 'to be enough'. {X に足[た]る Y} means 'Y that is sufficient for X / worthy of X': {信頼[しんらい]するに足[た]る人物[じんぶつ]} 'a person worthy of trust', {証明[しょうめい]するに足[た]る証拠[しょうこ]} 'evidence sufficient to prove it'.

The negative {〜に足[た]りない} means 'not worth X'. The fixed phrase {取[と]るに足[た]りない} 'trivial, not worth bothering about' is very common.

**Register:** formal and written — reports, legal language, essays. {取[と]るに足[た]りない} also appears in everyday conversation.

examples.jp: そんなことは取[と]るに足[た]りない問題[もんだい]だ。
examples.en: That's a trivial problem.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は信頼[しんらい]するに足[た]る人物[じんぶつ]だ。
examples.en: He is a man who can be trusted.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の主張[しゅちょう]を裏付[うらづ]けるに足[た]る証拠[しょうこ]は見[み]つからなかった。
examples.en: No evidence sufficient to back up his claim was found.

examples.jp: 満足[まんぞく]に足[た]る結果[けっか]とは言[い]えないが、一定[いってい]の成果[せいか]はあった。
examples.en: It can't be called a satisfying result, but there was some progress.

points.notes: Compare {〜に値[あたい]する} 'worth (doing)': {一読[いちどく]に値[あたい]する} 'worth reading'. {〜に足[た]る} focuses on sufficiency, {〜に値[あたい]する} on value.

quiz.q: その報告書[ほうこくしょ]には、信用[しんよう]する＿＿データが一[ひと]つもなかった。
quiz.en: There was not a single piece of data in that report worthy of trust.

quiz.q: 小[ちい]さなミスなど、気[き]にするに＿＿。
quiz.en: Small mistakes aren't worth worrying about.

points.title: 〜でなくてなんだろう
points.meaning: if this isn't X, what is?; this is surely X
points.structure: Noun + でなくてなんだろう(か) / でなくてなんであろう(か)
points.explanation:
A rhetorical question: 'If this is not X, then what is it?' — meaning 'this is X, without doubt'. The writer describes something striking, then labels it with strong emotion: love, fate, courage, a miracle, abuse, injustice.

The noun is usually abstract and weighty: {愛[あい]}, {運命[うんめい]}, {奇跡[きせき]}, {勇気[ゆうき]}, {悲劇[ひげき]}, {差別[さべつ]}.

**Register:** literary and rhetorical — essays, speeches, novels, impassioned editorials. You will almost never hear it in conversation; if you used it at a party, people would think you were giving a speech.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]が命[いのち]をかけて子[こ]どもを救[すく]ったのは、勇気[ゆうき]でなくてなんだろう。
examples.en: He risked his life to save a child — if that isn't courage, what is?

examples.jp: 何十年[なんじゅうねん]も離[はな]れていた二人[ふたり]が偶然[ぐうぜん]再会[さいかい]した。これが運命[うんめい]でなくてなんだろうか。
examples.en: Two people separated for decades met again by chance. If that isn't fate, what is?

examples.jp: 自分[じぶん]の夢[ゆめ]を捨[す]ててまで家族[かぞく]を支[ささ]えた母[はは]の生[い]き方[かた]は、愛[あい]でなくてなんだろう。
examples.en: My mother gave up her own dreams to support our family. What could that be but love?

examples.jp: 子[こ]どもに食[た]べ物[もの]を与[あた]えず放置[ほうち]するのは、虐待[ぎゃくたい]でなくてなんであろう。
examples.en: Leaving a child without food — if that isn't abuse, what is?

points.notes: {なんであろう} is even more literary than {なんだろう}. The pattern always expresses the writer's strong conviction.

quiz.q: 一度[いちど]も会[あ]ったことのない人々[ひとびと]のために一生[いっしょう]を捧[ささ]げる。これが愛[あい]＿＿。
quiz.en: Devoting your whole life to people you've never met — if that isn't love, what is?

quiz.q: 十年[じゅうねん]もの研究[けんきゅう]の末[すえ]に生[う]まれたこの発明[はつめい]は、努力[どりょく]の結晶[けっしょう]で＿＿なんだろう。
quiz.en: This invention, born of ten years of research, is surely the fruit of hard work.

points.title: 〜てしかるべきだ
points.meaning: should (naturally); deserves to; it's only right that
points.structure: Verb て-form + しかるべきだ / しかるべき + Noun (appropriate ...)
points.explanation:
{しかるべき} (from classical {然[しか]る} 'to be so' + {べき}) means 'appropriate, as it should be'. {〜てしかるべきだ} means 'it would be only right / natural for X to happen': {もっと評価[ひょうか]されてしかるべきだ} 'deserves to be more highly regarded'.

It's often used with passive verbs to argue that something deserves to happen but hasn't yet — giving it a slightly critical edge. With {〜てしかるべきだった}, it criticises something that should have happened.

As an adjective, {しかるべき} means 'appropriate, proper': {しかるべき措置[そち]} 'appropriate measures', {しかるべき人[ひと]} 'the proper person'. This is common in business and official language.

**Register:** formal; editorials, business, official statements.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]の功績[こうせき]は、もっと評価[ひょうか]されてしかるべきだ。
examples.en: His achievements deserve far more recognition.

examples.jp: 消費者[しょうひしゃ]には、正確[せいかく]な情報[じょうほう]が提供[ていきょう]されてしかるべきだ。
examples.en: Consumers ought to be provided with accurate information.

examples.jp: 本来[ほんらい]なら、もっと早[はや]く対策[たいさく]が取[と]られてしかるべきだった。
examples.en: By rights, countermeasures should have been taken much sooner.

examples.jp: 問題[もんだい]が確認[かくにん]され次第[しだい]、しかるべき措置[そち]を講[こう]じます。
examples.en: As soon as the problem is confirmed, we will take appropriate measures.

points.notes: Compare plain {〜べきだ}: {しかるべきだ} sounds more objective, as if it's simply the natural state of things.

quiz.q: これだけ努力[どりょく]したのだから、彼女[かのじょ]は報[むく]われて＿＿。
quiz.en: She's worked so hard; she deserves to be rewarded.

quiz.q: ミスを犯[おか]した以上[いじょう]、責任者[せきにんしゃ]は＿＿処分[しょぶん]を受[う]けるべきだ。
quiz.en: Since a mistake was made, the person in charge should receive appropriate disciplinary action.
